reason: Prior timing results are noisy and none promote a change, so they provide no reliable winner. I rank the 513-float scratch pitch first because it is a bounded, isolated address-layout test with a clear before/after: 512-float row starts become 513-float row starts, with matching allocation and K-loop strides. The supplied cache sizes do not establish a conflict, so this is a testable hypothesis, not a predicted gain. Next are output-store scheduling and operand scheduling changes that preserve the tile shape and K arithmetic; prefetch is less certain and can add traffic. Packing and traversal proposals have larger lifetime, address, or added-work risks; the 64x32 traversal already exists. All proposals require fresh paired measurements and correctness validation before drawing conclusions.
